Title: Melee Weapon and Q about Parity Shift

Messages.Author: Marko Puumalainen
Messages.Body:
I've been amused to read articles about chainsaws being melee weapons
or not. For me the definition of "melee weapon" is perfectly clear:

Melee weapon is a weapon that does damage proportional to the strength
of the bearer (in real life, not vampires strength). All weapons like
knives, swords, clubs, nunchakus, slings, boomerangs, etc. are melee
weapons even if they did ranged damage.

Weapons that need gunpowder, motors or any source of power other than
hand power are not melee weapons. For example, Ivory bow is not a melee
weapon because it's strike does not depend on the strength of the bearer
but uses the bow to give speed to the arrow.

Any comments on this definition?

Could someone give a latest ruling on Parity Shift.
Does "that blood" refer to the whole pool of the opponent, or just the
difference between my pool and hers?

))marko
--
Never try to be amusing and order something like a
"pint of dishwater". Judging by the state of some
of our larger brewers' beers, you just might get it.
The Surrey Pub Guide

Messages.Author: Duncan A McEwen
Messages.Body:
I just want to put in my two sense worth on this whole card backs fiasco.
I am very disappointed in WoTC. Jyhad was the best name because it told
what the game was really about. If the marketing had tried they could have
made it ovious that the game was about vampires. I feel the change is really
bad.
I do wander if the change is partly because of Jyhads success versus
Magic. WoTC should reallize that they scored big with Magic and that most
of the furture products will probobly never do as well. If they expect new

when a product doesn't go as good as magic they change it, tehy will have

you that we will not buy the new cards do to this change. I will bet
at some point the two types af card backs will become outlawed at
tournements. I am very sorry to see this happen.

Sorry for whining so much but I think alot of you agree with me.
Duncan McEwen

Messages.Body:

[explaination of 'melee' weapon elided]

Peace Marko,

I don't believe that the problem is whether Chainsaw _is_ a melee weapon,
it is whether it _should be_ a melee weapon for balance purposes. Why
use a Chainsaw when a Shotgun is better (and more common)?

> Could someone give a latest ruling on Parity Shift.
> Does "that blood" refer to the whole pool of the opponent, or just the
> difference between my pool and hers?

The official ruling is X is the number of Meths in play. X may exceed the
difference between pools. So, yes, you may oust someone with this card.

Nil carborundum illigitimi,

Messages.Author: Jeremy York
Messages.Body:
Duncan A McEwen (mce...@tools.ecn.purdue.edu) wrote:
: I am very disappointed in WoTC. Jyhad was the best name because it told

: what the game was really about.

Ask a typical comic/gaming/goth/sf person, who is unfamiliar with the
game, what a Jyhad is. You'll either get an answer of Holy War, or
an answer of "some kind of extremist Islamic terrorist campaign".
Where are the vampires there?

: If the marketing had tried they could have

: made it ovious that the game was about vampires.

Perhaps. But packaging has to do a lot of the selling in the
gaming industry. And if the packaging doesn't say anything about
vampires, well...and if you have to add in extra text that's even
more eye-catching than the title...why not just change the title.

: I do wander if the change is partly because of Jyhads success versus
: Magic.

I can't speak for WotC but I really doubt this. They knew from the
outset that they were pitching this game towards a more mature
crowd, a more specialized market niche. I doubt that they think
of it in those comparative terms, but rather, are just trying to
pitch the game as best they can.

: Speaking for several people here at Purdue university I can tell

: you that we will not buy the new cards do to this change.

And why is that? I really don't understand this strong, harsh reaction
I keep reading about. If you can't come up with some guidelines among
your friends for reasonable ways to mix cards, and trust them to
abide by them, I think you need new gaming friends.

(Guidelines I'd suggest :
Crypt should be all one printing
If mixing two printings in library, shouldn't have over
75% of cards of one printing be of a particular
type (example of an infraction - mostly Jyhad cards,
but all new printing cards are protean cards)
)

: I will bet

: at some point the two types af card backs will become outlawed at
: tournements. I am very sorry to see this happen.

I bet mixed decks may become outlawed at tournaments...but how
many Jyhad tournaments have you been to or seen? Are they the
main reason you play the game?

: Sorry for whining so much but I think alot of you agree with me.

I think a lot of you are over-reacting. Many people proclaimed
gloom and doom when the beta Magic cards turned out to have a
different shape corner. Yet ever since I and others have played
mixed alpha/post-alpha cards in decks without much problem or
concern; I have yet to play against someone I was sure was
taking advantage of the card shape difference to cheat. And if
I did, I would tell them what I thought of what they were doing,
and not play with them any more. Simple as that. Anyway, that
change did not bring about the end of Magic as we know it.

Now that tournaments are getting to be a big deal, concern about
unsportsmanlike players (eg assholes) have prompted most organizers
to say mixed alpha/post-alpha decks are not ok. Fine. So eventually,
if Jyhad ever gets to the point where there are (m)any tournaments
going on, somebody will abuse the card back thing, and people will
start restricting mixed decks. Not the end of the world by any
means!

I'm not in bed with WotC, and I'm not exactly smitten with
this name change thing, but I can understand it, and more importantly,
I'm trying to think about what it will realistically mean and
whether it matters much. I'd advise folks to choke back their
knee jerk reactions for a moment and consider the same...
--
Jeremy (bea...@netcom.com, bea...@delphi.com)

Messages.Author: William Jockusch
Messages.Body:
The idea of cracking down on players who abuse the fact that they are
allowed to use both kinds of card backs strikes me as somewhat
unworkable. How do you know if someone is taking advantage of the
different card backs or not? It seems just about impossible to prove.

Suggestion: Why not just allow players to have mixed backs in their decks
and make the information conveyed by this a legitimate part of the game?
This would circumvent the above problem. I do realize it could create new
problems, as the older, hard to obtain card backs might become more valuable
than the new ones, but I can't imagine this could possibly get too far out
of hand as has happened with magic.

William

>a .44 than when I don't. (Unless I'm laying down cover fire while

Try to view the gun not as using it to run away from the combat, but to fire
at the opposing minion before the combat gets to close range in the
first place. Using a gun in the second round of the combat rather than the
first doesn't involve using the gun to run away, either; assume the vampires
get separated a bit in the course of pressing but then normally close to
hand-to-hand, and in this case you again have one vampire sniping at the other
before the combat comes back to close range.

Messages.Author: Alan Kwan

In article <beanishD...@netcom.com> bea...@netcom.com (Jeremy York) writes:

>Now that tournaments are getting to be a big deal, concern about

>to say mixed alpha/post-alpha decks are not ok.

So you talk about sportsmanship. As far as I know, im most sports
they have explicit rules to punish unsportsmanly behaviour. For
example, in the last World Cup Soccer, they were much more stricter
on fouls.

It's always MNSHO that a game (i.e. the game designers) has the
responsibility to prohibit/discourage "unsportsmanly" behavior,
by prohibiting them in the rules, invoking penalties, or structuring
the game so that such behaviour leads to the player losing.
V:tES balantly violates this basic game design consideration by
changing the card backs, so that players can gain an advantage
in an "unsportsmanly" manner (marked cards). And this is IMNSHO
a completely unnecessary move.

Messages.Author: Aaron Mandelbaum

>breaks down (yielding to game mechanics) after the first round (how does
>one quickly get to the rooftop to continue this fight?), but it's a
>nice concept.

I think the idea is that it takes the other vampire two turns to close range,
since you start VERY far away. The free maneuver is intended to simulate
starting the fight from a distance, not moving away. Since shotguns,
flamethrowers, and bows (used by unskilled people) are not long-range
weapons, they don't get a maneuver.

It doesn't really make sense, based on how combat works, but from looking at
the weapons it looks like that's how they decided which got them.

--
Aaron Mandelbaum

backs also? If they've already bought the game, then they know what it's
about; if someone is just seeing the game being played, they'll also
easily see that its about vampires, and not about Islamic wars.

it, you decide to alienate all the people who have already bought it.
Doesn't seem like good business sense to me.

>The Convocation has no plans to outlaw decks with mixed card backs.

Yes, and I'm sure you had no plans to outlaw Magic decks with Alpha cards
in them when Beta first came out. But you eventually did. How do I know
that you won't eventually decide that Jyhad has to go?

I have always championed WOTC to my friends who claim that it is an
insensitive company. I have stated that WOTC is not intentionally trying

Peace Jeremy,

If packaging is the problem, then they should change the packageing (boxes,
packs, display stands) and leave the card backs alone. There is NO need to
change the card backs if it is all about marketting (which Tom has said it
is), so either a) it ISN'T all about marketting or b) WotC is trying to force
the established customers to buy more cars or c) WotC is stupid. Take your
pick.

> : Speaking for several people here at Purdue university I can tell

> : you that we will not buy the new cards do to this change.
>

> And why is that? I really don't understand this strong, harsh reaction
> I keep reading about. If you can't come up with some guidelines among
> your friends for reasonable ways to mix cards, and trust them to
> abide by them, I think you need new gaming friends.

Given history as it relates to CCGs in general, I predict that the old cards
will become outlawed (due to problems with mixed decks) just like Alphas
were. "Friendly play" often mirrors "tourney play" (you fight the way you
train), so people will start following the tourney rules (just like they
do in Mt$ [when was the last time you saw a Magic deck that wasn't tourney
legal?]) and this will obsolese the Jyhad backed cards. I'm sure (from
reading other people's posts) that /many/ players feel this will happen too.
That is why the majority of players are up in arms over the card back change.
The know what the inevitable result will be and they don't like it. It has
nothing to do with trusting your friends. It has to do with tourney rules
becoming the standard (which they do) and what effect that will have on
all the older cards.

> (Guidelines I'd suggest :
> Crypt should be all one printing
> If mixing two printings in library, shouldn't have over
> 75% of cards of one printing be of a particular
> type (example of an infraction - mostly Jyhad cards,
> but all new printing cards are protean cards)
> )

This is Jyhad, we don't need no steenkeeng card limits.

> : I will bet

> : at some point the two types af card backs will become outlawed at
> : tournements. I am very sorry to see this happen.
>

> I bet mixed decks may become outlawed at tournaments...but how
> many Jyhad tournaments have you been to or seen? Are they the
> main reason you play the game?

See above for why you have just supported my argument.

> : Sorry for whining so much but I think alot of you agree with me.
>
> I think a lot of you are over-reacting. Many people proclaimed
> gloom and doom when the beta Magic cards turned out to have a
> different shape corner. Yet ever since I and others have played
> mixed alpha/post-alpha cards in decks without much problem or
> concern; I have yet to play against someone I was sure was
> taking advantage of the card shape difference to cheat. And if
> I did, I would tell them what I thought of what they were doing,
> and not play with them any more. Simple as that. Anyway, that
> change did not bring about the end of Magic as we know it.

The Alpha run of Magic was much smaller than the run of Jyhad. The player
base was much smaller. It is a different scenario.

> Now that tournaments are getting to be a big deal, concern about
> unsportsmanlike players (eg assholes) have prompted most organizers

> to say mixed alpha/post-alpha decks are not ok. Fine. So eventually,
> if Jyhad ever gets to the point where there are (m)any tournaments
> going on, somebody will abuse the card back thing, and people will
> start restricting mixed decks. Not the end of the world by any
> means!

Yes, it will be for the older cards (see above).

> I'm not in bed with WotC, and I'm not exactly smitten with
> this name change thing, but I can understand it, and more importantly,
> I'm trying to think about what it will realistically mean and
> whether it matters much. I'd advise folks to choke back their
> knee jerk reactions for a moment and consider the same...

I don't "knee jerk", Jeremy. Ask others. They'll tell you. This is a
Bad Thing (TM) and it may force me out of CCGs permanently.
